# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Given the following project structure:

 - Project A
    - `ProjectA.MyType`

 - Project B
    - References
        - Project A
    - Package References
        - MessagePack
    
I need to have a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for type `ProjectA.MyType` generated **inside Project B** instead of Project A, because the latter has no (and cannot have) reference to MessagePack nuget package.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that will work for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.

For example:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

That's it. The class does not even need to declare a body (no `{` and `}`), because the actual implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives:

1 - Use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes. This is too limited IMO, as it cannot have `Union` and other features.

2 - Allow the generator and analyzers to work with user-defined versions of the MessagePack attributes. This would be similar to how you can declare dummy versions of BCL attributes that the C# compiler expects, such as [`[IsExternalInit]`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67687186/643085) or `[ModuleInitializer]`. With this, I could simply copy and paste the attribute definitions for MessagePack attributes such as `[Key]` into my Project A, and have the source-generated formatter (as described above) pick them.

3 - Source-generate the attributes themselves using [`IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext.RegisterPostInitializationOutput`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md#outputting-values) instead of them existing in the `MessagePack.Annotations` assembly. This would allow using the attributes without adding an additional runtime dependency. Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.

## Motivation

Project A is really a library (Nuget package), and I really want to keep it minimal. It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.

story.summary: Adds a public `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute to MessagePack.Annotations. When a `partial` class carries this attribute and implements `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`, the source generator writes the formatter body into that class and registers it in `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. `T` can live in an assembly that has no MessagePack reference. By default `T` is serialized contractless: public read-write members go into a string-keyed map, ordered by name. An optional `SurrogateType` names a type in the consuming project whose `[Key]`/`[IgnoreMember]` attributes define the keys instead. Four new error diagnostics (MsgPack019–022) are added, plus README and analyzer docs, a new dependency-free test assembly, execution tests and generator diagnostic tests.
story.why: REQ-2129 asks for a way to generate a formatter in Project B for a type in Project A, which cannot reference MessagePack. The requirement suggests this attribute on partial formatter classes. It leaves open how keys are chosen and lists three options. The agent picked a fourth design: contractless by default, plus a surrogate type in the consuming assembly.
touches_beyond_requirement: New public type `GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute` with a `SurrogateType` property in the shipped Annotations assembly (S3 fail).
Four new user-visible error rules MsgPack019–MsgPack022, with release notes and docs (S4 fail).
A surrogate-type design for keys, which is not one of the three alternatives in the issue.
The shared formatter templates (`FormatterTemplate.tt` and `StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt`) now emit `partial class` for user-declared formatters.
Hand-written formatter discovery in GeneratorUtilities now skips classes that carry the new attribute.
The MapModeExecutionTests project now excludes the new execution test files.
story.confidence_overview: High confidence that the basic path works: a contractless class or struct and a surrogate with int keys, from a separate assembly with no MessagePack reference, round-trip and get registered in the resolver. Execution tests exercise these. Medium confidence on edge paths that have no tests: string-key surrogates at runtime, duplicate keys, missing keys, classes without a parameterless constructor, generic data types, callback receivers. No generated-source snapshots are included, so the emitted code is not shown. The key design and the public API are product decisions the human needs to make.

findings.description: Claim C4 disputed: First, named test ContractlessClassNullRoundTrips (GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypesTests.cs lines 37-41) only serializes and deserializes null (default(ExternalPerson)) and does not test member discovery, string keys, or ordinal ordering; meanwhile ContractlessClassUsesStringKeysForPublicReadWriteMembers only tests a flat class with auto-properties already declared in alphabetical order (ExternalPerson.cs lines 7-15), leaving fields, base-type members, static members, and indexers untested. Second, IsPublicReadWrite (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs lines 279-281) matches any property whose SetMethod is public, which also includes init-only properties ({ get; init; }, handled at line 219), not strictly read-write properties.

Claim C6 disputed: First, MsgPack019 is only checked on the formatter declaration itself via IsPartial (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs lines 47 and 293-299) and does not check containing types; if a partial formatter is nested in a non-partial outer class, MsgPack019 is not reported (despite doc/analyzers/MsgPack019.md line 26) and generated code fails with CS0260. Second, record classes are valid targets for AttributeTargets.Class, but MessagePackGenerator.cs line 31 filters node is ClassDeclarationSyntax, silently ignoring non-partial or invalid record formatters with zero diagnostics. Third, the cited range GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs lines 47-81 omits where MsgPack022 is actually reported (lines 190-198).

`SurrogateType` is cast with `as INamedTypeSymbol`. A non-named type (for example `typeof(int[])`) or an error type turns into null, and the generator silently falls back to contractless mode with no diagnostic. The result is a different wire format from what the user asked for.

`GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect` runs twice per formatter: once for the model and once for diagnostics. The diagnostics pipeline combines each request with the full CompilationProvider, so it re-runs on every compilation change. This is an IDE performance cost; incremental caching is effectively lost for this path.

The existing descriptors NoDeserializingConstructor, DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys (L185) and KeysMustBeUnique (L202) are created without message arguments. If their message formats contain placeholders, the diagnostic text will be wrong or malformed. Only the MsgPack005 path is covered by a test.

`needsCast` only looks at explicit interface implementations on the type itself, not on its base types. The same flag is used for both the before and after callbacks. A callback receiver implemented explicitly on a base class, or only one callback implemented explicitly, may produce wrong generated code. This path is untested.

MsgPack019–022 are listed in the analyzer's SupportedDiagnostics, but the analyzer never reports them; only the source generator does. Users who rely on the analyzer alone, or on live IDE analysis, will not see these errors from the analyzer.

Test gaps: no generated-source snapshot shows what the generator emits; the string-key surrogate path is never executed at runtime. No tests cover MsgPack021 for generic types, KeysMustBeUnique, a surrogate member missing `[Key]`, or a class without a parameterless constructor. The issue's body-less `partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;` syntax is not exercised either.

Explicit IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver detection is always false: in Roslyn, an explicit interface implementation method's IMethodSymbol.Name includes the qualified interface prefix (e.g. 'MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize'), so m.Name == 'OnBeforeSerialize' || m.Name == 'OnAfterDeserialize' never matches when m.ExplicitInterfaceImplementations.Length > 0 (and type.GetMembers() also misses base-class implementations). If a formatted type implements IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver explicitly, needsCast is false and the generated formatter emits direct member calls that fail to compile with CS1061.

Collect validates the formatted data type (non-generic, non-abstract, accessible, parameterless constructor) but never validates those properties on the user-declared formatter symbol itself. If the formatter class is abstract, generic (or nested inside a generic type), private inside a partial outer type, or lacks an accessible parameterless constructor, the generator emits a GeneratedMessagePackResolver entry that instantiates new <Formatter>() and fails to compile with CS0144, CS0305, CS0122, or CS7036 instead of reporting a diagnostic.

IsPartial checks only the formatter class declaration and not symbol.ContainingType recursively. Nesting a partial formatter inside a non-partial outer type bypasses MsgPack019 (contradicting doc/analyzers/MsgPack019.md line 26) and produces invalid partial outer type declarations that fail compilation with CS0260.

CreateSurrogateMembers accepts negative integer keys such as [Key(-1)] because 'key is not (int or string)' does not check intKey >= 0, passing a negative IntKey into ObjectSerializationInfo.Create where non-negative array slot indices are assumed.

If the formatted type declares a C# 'required' property or field that is omitted or marked [IgnoreMember] on SurrogateType (or is a required get-only/non-public-setter member skipped in contractless mode), the generated Deserialize method constructs 'new T()' without initializing that required member, failing compilation with CS9035.

CreateSurrogateMembers enumerates GetInstanceMembers(surrogate), which returns all non-static fields and properties regardless of accessibility; any private helper field or property on the surrogate class triggers MsgPack004 (MemberNeedsKey) unless annotated with [IgnoreMember].

SurrogateType extraction uses 'as INamedTypeSymbol'; if a user specifies a non-named type such as SurrogateType = typeof(int[]), Surrogate becomes null and the generator silently falls back to contractless mode instead of reporting an invalid surrogate type.
